what: Above white silk (two layers of low-noise folds), five cut gems (cushion·oval·baguette·square·drop, with per-facet broken light + two sparkles + a white rim) float, each spinning and bobbing up and down by .06. On the floor, each gem gets a light-refraction pattern in its own color (moving cell edges) and a shadow cast to the lower right. The view tilts following the mouse at 5% per frame (±.12). Hovering a gem lifts it .4 forward and enlarges it 8%, with an 8px dot and a 1.2s spreading ring above it, firing fx:hover, and pressing fires fx:pick. fx:state { focus: n } Once chosen, that gem comes forward to the center of the screen (1.6s) while the rest recede outward and blur

options.follow · tilt: Share of the view that follows the mouse (per frame) · tilt strength, default .05 · .12
options.focus: Approach time (sec) to the selected gem, default 1.6
options.[data-fx-part=gem]: One gem (exactly, max 5) — data-name (name), data-shape (cushion·oval·baguette·square·pear), data-at="x y size"(screen position -1~1). This element becomes the dot above the hovered gem and receives the gem’s screen position via --fx-x · --fx-y
options.--fx-gem-1 … --fx-gem-5: Gem colors (style or css), default emerald · sapphire · topaz · ruby · deep navy — the color itself is the content, not a skin color
options.--fx-floor · --fx-floor-shade: Silk light surface · fold shadow, default --kf-bg and a color 18% darker
options.fx:hover · fx:leave · fx:pick: Event bubbling up from the element — detail { index, name }

note: The original draws a gem 3D model (glb) and a pre-baked caustics image with its own WebGL engine. Here it is our own faceted shape carved up from an outline, plus shader math (facet light · sparkle · cell-boundary pattern). It does not draw when off-screen or in a hidden tab. With reduced motion it neither spins nor wobbles
